headline: AN UNUSUAL OUTBREAK OF MEASLES IN HAWAII, 1936-37
blurb: A measles epidemic in the Territory of Hawaii began in November 1936 and peaked in March 1937, when 2,558 cases were reported.

headline: Measles -- Hawaii
source: CDC, Morbidity and Mortality Weekly Report
blurb: Between May 5 and June 29, 1984, 106 measles cases were reported on the island of Kauai, and 49% were in children under 5 years old.

headline: Premarital rubella screening program: from identification to vaccination of susceptible women in the state of Hawaii.
blurb: In a study of Hawaii's premarital rubella screening program, 52% of women who were mailed a letter urging vaccination had been vaccinated three months later, compared with 24% of women who were not sent one.

headline: Hepatitis A Outbreak 2016
blurb: On August 15, 2016, Hawaii health officials named raw scallops served at Genki Sushi restaurants on Oahu and Kauai as a likely source of a hepatitis A outbreak that reached 292 confirmed cases.

headline: Hawai‘i Department of Health declares mumps outbreak over
blurb: Hawaii's health department declared the end of a statewide mumps outbreak that began in March 2017 and included 1,009 people.

headline: New Immunization Requirements for School Attendance
blurb: Hawaii announced updated immunization requirements for school starting in fall 2020, including Tdap, HPV and meningococcal vaccines for all seventh graders.

headline: MEASLES CASE CONFIRMED IN CHILD ON OʻAHU — DOH NOTIFIES PUBLIC OF MEASLES EXPOSURE LOCATIONS
blurb: Hawaii's health department confirmed a measles case in an unvaccinated child under 5 years old on Oahu.

headline: DOH RESPONDING TO INCREASED PERTUSSIS CASES IN HAWAIʻI IN 2025
blurb: Hawaii's health department had identified 203 whooping cough cases as of July 31, 2025, compared with 84 cases in all of 2024.
